brief: Goldman Sachs forecasts September nonfarm payrolls rose 80k, below consensus of 88k but above the three-month average of 71k. It forecasts private payrolls at 75k versus consensus of 80k. Arguing for a stronger report: initial jobless claims averaged 204k, in line with August, the JOLTS layoff rate fell 0.1pp to 1.0%, Challenger-tracked layoffs fell 2k to 52k, and alternative big-data measures of job growth averaged 77k, up from 31k in August. Arguing for a weaker report: a late Labor Day this year has historically dragged September payrolls below trend, and August's reported strength was overstated by a combined 104k rebound in local education and leisure/hospitality payrolls that GS does not expect to repeat. Mixed signals: job openings held roughly flat, the Conference Board's labor differential fell 2.5pt to +1.7, and employer survey trackers rose but GS says that signal has been unreliable since the pandemic. GS forecasts average hourly earnings up 0.2% month over month, below consensus of 0.3%, and the unemployment rate edging down to 4.0% from 4.1% on falling continuing claims, though its broader slack tracker, at 4.6%, implies the labor market is softer than the headline rate suggests.
